subject: Model fit eval — discovery recap & acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@finlytics.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit eval — discovery recap & acceptance thresholds

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of customer problem
- Finlytics needs a production-grade inference stack for their financial insights assistant: fast response for short queries (<= 300 tokens) and robust handling of multi-step extraction tasks (tables, entity normalization) from SEC filings and earnings transcripts.
- Key non-functional: P95 latency <= 400ms for single-turn queries during peak (10 qps), strict audit logging and retention for regulated customers.

Model fit observations from discovery
- Your current in-house baseline (v1.3) is strong on domain-specific extraction but shows hallucination on numeric normalization prompts.
- Open community models show promising language coverage and hallucination reduction on generic prompts, but they vary widely on structured-extraction fidelity.

Proposed evaluation approach (attached: eval_playbook_v1.xlsx)
1) Core prompt set: run 600 prompts (200 classification/intent, 200 extraction/table, 200 numeric normalization) — I attached prompt-set-key-queries.jsonl
2) Benchmarks: run both proprietary baseline and two open candidates (Opena-13B-chat and Atlas-7B-q) across identical inference configs (same temperature, max_tokens, system prompts). Save per-prompt outputs and token-level latencies.
3) Acceptance thresholds (initial draft) — suggested minimums to consider an open model "parity candidate":
   - Intent accuracy >= 92% (micro F1)
   - Extraction exact-match >= 85% on table cell values
   - Average numeric normalization error <= 3.0% (relative)
   - No more than 2% quality regressions on prioritized prompts vs baseline
   - P95 latency for production config <= 450ms (we can tune batching)

Next steps / asks
- Sophie: please confirm the list of 20 priority customer prompts you mentioned and share the dataset location or sample exports (ops@finlytics.ai was referenced).
- Tom: can you provide the baseline inference logs for the last 2 weeks (token counts + latencies) so we can estimate cost delta when switching models?
- Marissa / Neha (internal): we'll need a quick cost-vs-latency proposal and a draft mutually agreed action plan for a 4-week eval window.

I attached a lightweight playbook and a sample benchmark CSV template (benchmark_summary_finlytics.csv). If the acceptance thresholds above look aggressive, we can calibrate them after the pilot run.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): exchange assets + access
- Week 1: run ingestion + smoke tests
- Week 2: baseline vs open candidates run
- Week 3: qualitative review + prompted regression triage
- Week 4: recommendation + capacity/cost proposal

I'll hold a 30-minute sync mid next week if that works for everyone.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- eval_playbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, evaluation checklist)
- prompt-set-key-queries.jsonl (100+ priority prompts)
- benchmark_summary_finlytics.csv (CSV template)

From: Sophie Grant <sophie@finlytics.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmetech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — discovery recap & acceptance thresholds

Thanks Marcus — this is great and very actionable. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority prompts: I'll export the 20 priority prompts today and drop to ops@finlytics.ai; they include many edge-case numeric prompts (currency conversions across rounds, pro-rata calculations).
- Baseline logs: we can export the last 14 days of inference telemetry (latency/token counts). I'll coordinate with Tom to share a secure link to the logs.
- Acceptance thresholds: the extraction exact-match >= 85% feels reasonable; numeric normalization <= 3% might be tight for open models initially. Can we allow a staged threshold (e.g., 3% target, 5% staging acceptable with explicit mitigation plan)?

Also, a quick heads-up: compliance will need a data flow diagram and a statement of where logs are retained (S3 region). We'll include that in the access package.

Sophie
Head of Product — Finlytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@finlytics.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — discovery recap & acceptance thresholds

Thanks Sophie — perfect. Quick follow-up:

1) Staged acceptance: happy to make numeric normalization staged: 5% acceptable for staging with a documented remediation plan (prompt engineering + small classifier for numeric normalization). If after the pilot the open model hits 3% -> we can prioritize rollout.

2) Benchmark candidates: we propose running three snapshots:
   - PropBaseline v1.3 (your in-house model)
   - CommunityCandidate-A (Opendawn-13B-chat, quantized where possible)
   - CommunityCandidate-B (Mistral-7B-instruct tuned)

3) Evaluation metrics & tooling: we'll produce a per-prompt diff report (exact-match, token-level latency, hallucination flags). The playbook includes a short rubric for "hallucination" classification.

4) Access: Sophie/Tom — when you share logs, please include a sample of masked customer PII so we can sanity-check regexes. We'll keep all artifacts in a shared S3 bucket with access logs and provide the compliance diagram (simple PNG) in the same folder.

5) Sync: propose Wed Jul 15 10:00 PT (30m) for intake and handoff to the evaluation team — invite sent to all.

Marissa / Neha: action items for internal team:
- Marissa: draft a cost delta estimate comparing production cost/p95 for each candidate (include quantized infer cost).
- Neha: prepare the evaluation runner config and the regression alert thresholds (we have an existing alert set in the console; need to map to Finlytics prompts).

I'll upload the playbook and prompt set to the shared drive.

Regards,
Marcus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 22:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — discovery recap & acceptance thresholds

Quick internal note:

- I'll spin up the eval runner tomorrow morning using the attached prompt set. Plan: batch at 8 concurrent requests to mirror Finlytics peak but keep single-request latencies visible (we log both).
- For acceptance/regression alerts: I'm setting an auto-alert if any key prompt drops >4% extraction EM vs your reported baseline; will create a Slack webhook for the Finlytics shared channel.
- Cost estimate (prelim): Opendawn-13B-chat (quantized) is ~0.45x cost of baseline per-token but we need to include additional engineering for numeric post-processing; Mistral-7B-instruct is cheaper (~0.30x) but may need heavier prompt engineering to hit extraction EM. I'll send a short spreadsheet by EOD.

I'll also flag the three prompts we think will be the hardest (two numeric normalization, one nested table extraction).

-Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
